name: PW Digital Gateway
note: Approved in 2023 (4-3-1) but the rezoning was judicially voided over defective hearing notice; county and developer dropped their appeals in 2026, ending the project as approved.

name: Plaza 500 (Lincolnia)
note: By-right data center on the 34-acre 6299 Edsall Road site; the required substation faces a Fairfax County Planning Commission Public Facilities (2232) review on Sept 24, 2026 amid organized opposition.

name: Project Iron Spur
note: ~129-acre hyperscale campus proposed across from Rural Hall town hall; Forsyth County Planning Board recommended denial. Commissioners held the public hearing July 30, 2026 - decision pending.

name: Meta Hyperion
note: Approved and under construction - a ~5 GW, ~$27B campus. Louisiana approved new Entergy natural-gas generation to serve it; ratepayer cost allocation is the live fight, not the siting.

name: Burkhalter Road data center (4AM Development)
note: Two-story 230,000 sq ft data center plus a 32,000 sq ft substation on ~26.5 acres at 6539 Burkhalter Road (R-4 residential to Office & Business rezoning). Planning Commission recommended approval 5-1; City Council decides Aug 18, 2026. Bulloch County, separately, has been extending data-center moratoriums.

name: West Erwin Street data center (Barrio Resources)
note: Special use permit for a bitcoin-mining data center on ~1.92 acres near downtown (W. Erwin St & N. Ross Ave) denied 5-2 by the Planning & Zoning Commission - staff found it inconsistent with the Future Land Use Map and comprehensive plan, after resident opposition over water, noise, and proximity to homes. Applicant may appeal.

name: Aligned Data Centers - Pataskala industrial park
note: 200 MW campus in three buildings on ~89 acres at Broad St SW & Mink St SW. Planning & Zoning recommended rejection 5-2 after protests filled City Hall; City Council decides Aug 25, 2026 (5:30 p.m.). Council has separately advanced a ballot measure that could ban large data centers.

name: King of Prussia campus (MLP Ventures)
note: Five-site, 4.6M sq ft campus across King of Prussia. Applications were filed in early March 2026, roughly ten days before Upper Merion's new data-center ordinance took effect - exempting them from its residential buffer, noise, and water-use rules. The township Planning Commission voted against three of the proposals in July 2026; review continues amid packed hearings and organized opposition.

name: AWS Calvert Technology Center
note: Eight data center buildings (266,000-332,000 sq ft each) proposed at 1650 Calvert Cliffs Parkway on Constellation-owned parcels near the Calvert Cliffs nuclear plant. AWS formally withdrew the concept site plan on Aug 4, 2026 - after first-round county review comments and before any resubmission. Timeline documented on the county's own project page.

name: xAI Colossus
note: Operating and expanding (~$20B, ~2 GW ambition). The live fight is air quality: on-site gas turbines in southwest Memphis - an area already failing federal ozone standards - drew a Clean Air Act suit. Environmental groups' tracking put unpermitted turbines at 27 in Feb 2026, growing to 59 by mid-2026 across the Colossus complex (incl. Colossus 2 in Southaven, MS).
